summary: Use a thin Next.js Route Handler for browser SSE, a transport-neutral assistant generation use-case for shared policy, and separate provider/queue adapters. Cancellation and idle timeout belong to the generation orchestration; HTTP encoding and committed-header behavior belong to the inbound adapter.

tree.purpose: Valibot schemas for prompts and normalized generation events/results.
Transport-neutral error categories: validation, provider, cancellation, timeout, unexpected.
Shared generation orchestration: invokes the provider, resets an idle timer per provider event, propagates AbortSignal, classifies failures, and emits normalized events.
Provider seam exposing token/event streaming with an AbortSignal.
Application port for one-per-operation unexpected-failure reporting.
Maps normalized outcomes to retry, success, or dead-letter decisions.
Remote model implementation; translates provider protocol and failures into application-neutral results.
Sentry/logging implementation with redaction and operation-level deduplication.
Persistence for job status, attempts, final output, and dead-letter metadata.
POST Route Handler: authenticates, validates, composes dependencies, returns SSE, maps pre-commit failures, and handles post-commit in-band failure events.
Durable-job adapter; invokes the same generation use-case and applies retry/dead-letter policy.
Thin App Router entrypoint delegating to the inbound stream adapter.
Server-only composition root for provider, reporter, job ports, auth, and environment configuration.
Browser prompt UI consuming the SSE protocol and displaying tokens or safe failure messages.

flows: Browser: POST /api/assistant/stream -> authenticate and validate -> compose dependencies -> generateAssistant({prompt, signal: request.signal, emit}) -> remoteModelProvider.stream(signal) -> normalize token events -> SSE encoder -> browser.
Cancellation: browser disconnect/AbortSignal -> Route Handler signal -> generation signal -> provider request abort; classify cancellation without retry or duplicate failure reporting.

Idle timeout: start an inactivity timer for each generation; reset it whenever a provider event/token arrives; abort only after the configured idle interval. Do not use a whole-request deadline, so a successful stream may run indefinitely while active.
Provider failure before headers: provider adapter returns a normalized failure -> use-case classifies safe public error -> Route Handler returns the appropriate status and generic body.

Failure after headers: SSE stream pump catches the normalized/unexpected failure, reports an unexpected failure through the deduplicating reporter when applicable, emits one in-band failure event, then closes the stream.

Unexpected failure: the single application operation owns a report-once operation key; caught failures are reported before safe conversion. Route-level handling does not capture an already-reported error again.

Background job: queue -> assistant-worker -> authenticate/job-context validation -> generateAssistant with the same provider policy, cancellation, idle timeout, and error classification -> persist successful output -> acknowledge; retry transient provider/timeout failures within attempt limits; dead-letter permanent/auth/validation failures or exhausted retries.

decisions.rationale: The browser requires SSE headers, status codes, disconnect signals, and an HTTP streaming lifecycle.

decisions.choice: Transport-neutral use-case with an event sink
decisions.rationale: HTTP streaming and background jobs reuse provider invocation, cancellation, timeout, normalization, and failure classification without importing Next.js APIs.

decisions.choice: AbortSignal passed from inbound adapter through the provider port
decisions.rationale: Disconnect cancellation reaches the remote request and is distinguishable from provider failure.

decisions.choice: Idle timeout in the generation use-case
decisions.rationale: It aborts stalled providers while allowing arbitrarily long active streams.

decisions.choice: Normalize at the provider seam and expose only categorized application errors
decisions.rationale: Raw provider messages, credentials, stacks, and transport details never reach the browser or job payload.

decisions.choice: Injected failure-reporter port with operation-level deduplication
decisions.rationale: Both pre-commit and post-commit paths, plus worker handling, can share exactly-once reporting semantics.
Retry/dead-letter decisions remain consistent across worker implementations and provider error categories.

risks: SSE framing and stream cleanup must ensure the idle timer, provider reader, and abort listeners are released on completion, cancellation, and failure.
The remote provider must honor AbortSignal; otherwise cancellation may stop local work but leave the upstream request running.
Exactly-once telemetry is an operation-level guarantee implemented with a stable operation ID and deduplication store or bounded process-local guard.
Job retries require idempotency and persisted attempt state so a worker crash cannot duplicate final output or side effects.
